integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A satirical Brazilian street-news report in expressive stylized 3D cartoon animation. Rounded original adult human characters, clear appealing facial expressions, deliberately animated proportions, matte colorful clothing, chunky hands with five fingers, soft warm afternoon lighting, clean readable silhouettes. Not live action. Vertical composition. A peaceful but energetic gamers' rebellion outside a fictional electronics store in a Brazilian city square. No real brand names, real politicians, weapons, fire or injuries. Cardboard placards on wooden sticks, graphics of a graphics card, RAM sticks, a car and crossed-out bills. Main speakers remain large and legible on a phone, faces within the central safe area; crowd in the background. A few big rectangular pale cardboard signs with straight borders face camera in the foreground so final lettering can be composited exactly. Independent hand gestures, crowd footsteps and placard movement. The camera performs a gentle real sideways dolly with foreground signposts crossing faster than distant storefronts; never spins or hides speakers. One uninterrupted camera shot, no internal cuts, no subtitles, no news lower-thirds, no watermark. Only the indicated person speaks at each time; listening mouths remain closed. Spoken dialogue is natural contemporary Brazilian Portuguese with comic indignation, intelligible normal cadence, no invented extra words. Ambient crowd is softer than the interview. Music: none.
0.0-3.2s: Foreground protesters lift placards while the crowd chants in Brazilian Portuguese exactly <d>[Portuguese] Baixa a placa! Baixa a RAM!</d>. A woman reporter, medium brown skin, short dark curly bob, yellow jacket, blue jeans, holds a plain black microphone. An adult male gamer beside her has tan skin, short dark hair, small stubble, rectangular glasses, teal T-shirt with a small controller icon and dark jeans. Both stay planted, reporter screen left and interviewee screen right, same height. Behind them signs contain the slogans MINHA PLACA MINHA VIDA and MAIS RAM MENOS BOLETO; final exact typography is a separate graphic layer.
3.2-5.6s: Reporter turns toward the man and brings the microphone near his mouth, asks lightly but clearly <d>[Portuguese] Por que você veio protestar?</d>. The man listens first and looks at her microphone.
5.6-11.8s: The man starts restrained, then raises his real car keys in one hand on the word carro and says exactly <d>[Portuguese] Pra comprar uma placa de vídeo, eu tenho que vender o carro!</d>. The reporter follows the keys with her eyes; he keeps both feet grounded and keys never morph into a vehicle or another object.
11.8-15.083s: Reporter gives a single surprised side glance, the man holds up the keys with a resigned open-palm gesture; nearby protesters notice and react with one amused cheer, lift the signs and begin to move forward a small step. Continuing physical action through the last frame, with speaking completed before the final second. No repeated sentence or frozen ending. The car is only referred to and represented by keys, never sold or shown vanishing.
overall_soundscape: Clean female reporter and slightly exasperated warm adult male voice, Brazilian Portuguese. Synchronized lip motion only for the current speaker. Two clear initial crowd chants, soft street ambience, keys jingle when lifted, and a short crowd cheer after the punchline. No background dialogue under the critical line.
non_diegetic_music: None.
